headline: High-risk default interaction: Authelia can feed broad network-auth context into Kestra, which can write/execute workflows and externalize data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/OAuth and ForwardAuth outputs, while Kestra can read files/stdin and run declarative workflows. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not proven; the plausible bridge is manual or orchestrated handoff of auth-related content into Kestra parsing.
conditions: IF Authelia outputs are copied into Kestra workflow inputs or files
IF Kestra parses those inputs as instructions or templated workflow content
mitigations: Keep Authelia outputs out of Kestra-parsed fields
Use a strict schema for any handoff file
Disable ad hoc copy-paste between systems
Add a review step before Kestra consumes auth-related text

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/OAuth flows; Kestra reads/writes filesystem paths and can send data to many external services. A shared workspace is not documented, but if one exists, Kestra can move workflow inputs, logs, or artifacts outward, creating a realistic leakage path from Authelia-adjacent data.
conditions: IF both agents share a workspace or mounted volume
IF Authelia-related tokens, headers, or config files are placed where Kestra can read them
IF Kestra workflows forward those files or logs to external APIs
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Store secrets outside Kestra-readable paths
Redact auth material before workflow ingestion
Restrict Kestra outbound connectors for sensitive jobs
Rotate any credentials exposed in shared files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make broad network-auth decisions, and Kestra can execute shell, spawn subprocesses, write files, and use elevated privileges including root/docker.sock. That overlap creates a dangerous conflict if both touch the same mutable resources or deployment state; Kestra's write/execute surface is much broader than Authelia's, so collisions can be destructive.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem, container, or deployment namespace
IF Kestra workflows modify files or services that Authelia also depends on
IF no external locking or orchestration guard is present
mitigations: Put each agent in a separate namespace
Mount distinct writable directories
Disable root/docker.sock for routine runs
Add file or resource locks around shared state
Use read-only mounts for Authelia config

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions and identity assertions, and Kestra can act on inputs by running workflows, shell, and external integrations. If Kestra treats Authelia-derived output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated auth result can cascade into automated actions such as notifications, cloud calls, or data movement without verification.
conditions: IF Kestra consumes Authelia output as a trigger or variable source
IF no validation step checks the authenticity or freshness of that output
IF downstream tasks perform side effects such as email, cloud, or database actions
mitigations: Require signed or schema-validated handoff data
Insert a manual approval step for privileged workflows
Compare auth claims against an independent source
Log and alert on unexpected Authelia-to-Kestra triggers
Limit side-effecting tasks to allowlisted workflows

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Kestra explicitly touches logs, inputs, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Authelia handles authentication flows via OIDC/OAuth. If regulated identity data is routed through Kestra, retention and residency controls can diverge; the pair does not document matching compliance guarantees, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF regulated identity or access logs are routed through Kestra
IF Kestra retention or notification sinks differ from Authelia's identity-data handling
IF no documented DPA, residency, or retention alignment exists
mitigations: Classify identity data before routing it
Exclude regulated fields from Kestra logs
Set short retention on workflow logs and artifacts
Document residency and retention for both systems
Use separate tenants for regulated workflows
